collection.credit:
* V10 reputation, appointment, school and rivalry events: event prose
  and detailed branching by ChatGPT. Requested social outcomes and
  leadership roles, including ostracism, laughingstock, village idiot,
  mad scientist, trusted advisor, teacher and heads of professions:
  Lorsieab2. VV3–VV5-only Magic/Nature faction rule: Lorsieab2.

ledger.why: designer rule: magician and naturalist only in VV3-VV5 (the items' game gate)
titles are story only (rule 7); nursing parents are never harmed

(Subject) has excellent skill but poor teamwork. The leaders request a plan for improvement.
(Friend) has quietly mentored others for years. The record impresses the council.
Both are qualified; the decision rests on the office's current needs.
Apprentices praise (Subject)'s patience.
Several workers complain that (Friend) takes credit for others' work. The claims are checked.
The workers prefer a shared leadership arrangement.
A child nominates the village's pet lizard. The nomination is respectfully declined.
(Subject) organizes a complex project beautifully.
(Friend) handles a mistake with honesty and care.
Both perform well but disagree over priorities.
One candidate refuses to delegate and becomes exhausted; the leaders offer feedback.
(Subject) is appointed after demonstrating competence.
(Friend) is appointed after demonstrating competence.
Both are assigned complementary coordinating duties.
Neither is appointed; the leaders reopen nominations.
The responsible candidate admits wrongdoing and accepts a temporary bar from leadership.
A falsely accused candidate insists on a public correction before returning to work.
The investigation reveals poor record-keeping, not deliberate wrongdoing; the procedures are fixed.
The accused candidate is cleared. The accuser apologizes and corrects the rumor.
The candidate is cleared but declines the office, saying the process has exhausted (candidate.him/her).
The candidate accepts the appointment while requesting clearer future procedures.
The winner is jubilant; the loser is furious and refuses to attend the celebration.
The loser congratulates the winner sincerely, then cries alone later.
The winner admits to feeling frightened rather than triumphant.
The new coordinator's first act is to give the apprentices credit for their work.
The winner delivers a speech so long that an elderly villager falls asleep.
A disgraced candidate earns trust back over time through consistent work, not one grand apology.
The former rivals become effective colleagues without becoming friends.
The village remembers the appointment as a lesson in fairness rather than a triumph for one faction.
The new head appoints a former rival as an advisor, after discussing clear boundaries.
The loser declares the process corrupt and spends a week sulking. A child asks whether sulking counts as a profession.

intro.name: The office
intro.text: The village leaders announce that a respected senior worker will be selected to coordinate {A}. It is a responsibility, not a magical promotion in skill.

text_only.reason: the text says there is none; the office is story only (rule 7)

question.name: The candidates
question.text:
Two qualified candidates, (Subject) and (Friend), are nominated. They {respect each other|secretly despise each other|used to be friends|are parent and adult child|have been rivals since their apprenticeship}.
A third villager, (Third), is {a meticulous record-keeper|an opinionated elder|a worried apprentice|a former critic}.

choices.label: ASK THE WORKERS WHO KNOW THE CANDIDATES.

al1.text: The allegation is supported by records. The candidate receives a fair hearing and may be disqualified.

al2.text: The allegation is false and was spread by a rival.

al3.text: The allegation stems from a misunderstanding.

al4.text: Evidence remains inconclusive; the appointment is delayed rather than treating suspicion as guilt.

text_only.reason: the loser refuses to attend a celebration the story mentions; no celebration is asked for
